title: Experimental Auto review before each tool call
summary: An experimental `auto` permission mode runs with full access but has a reviewer model judge every tool call, including each tool call a program makes, before its body runs. There are no exemptions by tool name and no cached grants, and a denial never executes the body.
firstReason: It is a product permission mode built on the tool pipeline's pre-execute gate, which the Go design keeps. Its stated limit (direct effects inside a program are not reviewed) must be carried over as a stated limit.

title: Auto review asks the user after a denial
summary: When the session's approval policy is `ask`, an Auto review denial becomes a question to the person through the approval service instead of a final denial. A reviewer failure is reported as a failure, distinct from a denial, and the tool body does not run in either case.
firstReason: A person watching can overrule a misjudged denial without switching the whole session to full access, and failures stop being reported as refusals.

title: Agent terminals in the Web sidebar
summary: An experimental backend makes the agent's persistent terminals ordinary sidebar terminals that a person can watch. A terminal records who opened it; the person's first typed input takes control, after which agent writes, signals and closing are refused while reads continue.
firstReason: It unifies two terminal systems behind one controller and gives a clear rule for handing control over. Telling typed input apart from terminal-protocol replies stays a concern of the terminal island.

title: Headless caller authority for Auto review
summary: Auto review can be selected explicitly in headless, SDK and ACP hosts. Text whose recorded source is the user counts as instruction whether a human or a supervising program sent it; files, tool results and injected context never gain instruction authority, and task text cannot choose its own source.
firstReason: Authority by recorded source, not by message role, is the rule that makes a model reviewer safe against injected text. It is language-neutral.

title: Borrow Auto review inputs until serialization
summary: Proposal: the auto-review risk classifier stops copying and deep-freezing its input snapshot, because the only caller serializes it immediately.
firstReason: Exists only because of JavaScript: the saving is one array copy and one `Object.freeze` traversal. Go has no freeze step; whether the classifier copies or borrows a slice is an implementation detail of that component.
